task_family: ESRS E1 Climate Change; S1 Own Workforce; G1 Business Conduct
project_context: Transparent evidence-card RAG for AI-assisted CSRD / ESRS-style disclosure generation

design_notes.purpose: Run the twelve 2023-edition ESRS tasks as independent company-year-task cases through the existing W2 retrieval, shared generation and evaluation pipeline. E1 task records are copied unchanged; S1/G1 task selection remains provisional.
not_frozen_here: expanded task selection and evidence validation

tasks.task_name: Transition plan for climate change mitigation
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about the existence, content, implementation status, targets, actions, investments, and alignment claims of the company's climate transition plan.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: E1-1 is included because it tests strategic narrative grounding and high-risk overclaiming around transition-plan existence, implementation status, decarbonisation levers, investment support, and 1.5C or Paris-alignment claims.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: ESRS E1-1 concerns the undertaking's transition plan for climate change mitigation, including compatibility with the transition to a sustainable economy and limiting global warming to 1.5C where applicable.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The evidence-card corpus can plausibly support this task through PDF narrative cards describing climate strategy, transition plans, decarbonisation roadmaps, actions, targets, governance, and investments. PDF table-row evidence may support action or investment details when available.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about climate transition plans, decarbonisation strategy, transition roadmap, climate targets, actions, governance, investments, resources, and implementation status.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS E1-style disclosure paragraph about the company's transition plan using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: climate targets linked to the transition plan
resources, investments, CapEx, or OpEx linked to transition actions
1.5C, Paris-alignment, or science-based alignment claims only when explicitly evidenced
claim_risk_notes: over-claiming that a transition plan exists
unsupported 1.5C or Paris-alignment claim
planned versus implemented confusion
unsupported investment or resource claim
overly positive framing of transition-plan credibility

tasks.task_name: Actions and resources in relation to climate policies
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about climate actions, mitigation or adaptation measures, resources, investments, implementation status, and achieved or expected outcomes.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: E1-3 is included because it tests whether action-oriented disclosures are grounded in evidence about actual or planned measures, resources, implementation status, and claimed outcomes.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: ESRS E1-3 concerns actions and resources in relation to climate change policies, including key actions taken or planned and resources allocated to their implementation.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The evidence-card corpus can plausibly support this task through PDF narrative cards describing climate actions, energy-efficiency measures, renewable-energy procurement, operational changes, resource allocation, and action outcomes. PDF table-row cards may support action, investment, CapEx, OpEx, or performance tables when available.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about climate actions, mitigation measures, adaptation actions, resources, CapEx, OpEx, investments, implementation status, achieved outcomes, and expected or achieved emission reductions.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS E1-style disclosure paragraph about climate actions and resources using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: achieved or expected greenhouse gas emission reductions
claim_risk_notes: unsupported causal claims about actions causing emission reductions
planned versus completed action confusion
exaggerated scale of action
unsupported achieved or expected reduction claim
unsupported resource or investment claim

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about climate targets, baseline year, target year, covered scopes, reduction type, target boundary, progress, and validation claims.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: E1-4 is included because it tests target-specific grounding, including baseline years, target years, covered scopes, target type, progress claims, and unsupported validation or science-based target claims.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: ESRS E1-4 concerns targets related to climate change mitigation and adaptation, including target characteristics, baseline values, target periods, scope coverage, and progress where disclosed.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The evidence-card corpus can plausibly support this task through PDF narrative cards, PDF table-row cards, and CSV metric cards containing target descriptions, baseline values, emissions metrics, progress indicators, and related climate performance information.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about climate targets, greenhouse gas reduction targets, baseline years, target years, covered scopes, target type, target progress, and external validation if explicitly evidenced.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS E1-style disclosure paragraph about climate-related targets using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: SBTi or external validation only when explicitly evidenced
claim_risk_notes: target year and reporting year confusion
missing or incorrect baseline year
unsupported target progress claim
unsupported SBTi, science-based, or external validation claim
unclear scope or boundary coverage

tasks.task_name: Gross Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3 and total GHG emissions
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3, total GHG emissions, units, reporting year, methodology, and reporting boundary.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: E1-6 is included because it tests numeric, temporal, unit, and scope-boundary grounding across structured CSV metric evidence, PDF table-row evidence, and narrative methodology evidence.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: ESRS E1-6 concerns gross Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3 and total greenhouse gas emissions.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The evidence-card corpus can plausibly support this task through CSV metric cards containing structured emissions indicators, PDF table-row cards containing emissions tables, and PDF narrative cards describing methodology, boundary, and Scope 2 calculation approaches.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific numeric and methodological evidence for gross Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3 and total GHG emissions, including units, reporting boundary, and Scope 2 method where available.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS E1-style disclosure paragraph about GHG emissions using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
claim_risk_notes: numeric error
unit error
wrong reporting year
Scope 2 market-based versus location-based confusion
incomplete total emissions
boundary confusion

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about adopted workforce policies, their covered populations, labour and human-rights commitments, non-discrimination, equal opportunities, and occupational safety policy.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests whether policy existence, applicability and commitments remain grounded. Its focus is policy content and coverage; action implementation belongs to S1-4.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS S1, paragraphs 17-24. Policies related to own workforce.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: Historical human-resources, human-rights and safety sections are plausible narrative sources. Supplier-only policies cannot establish coverage of own workforce.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about adopted workforce policies, their covered populations, labour and human-rights commitments, non-discrimination, equal opportunities, and occupational safety policy.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS S1-style disclosure paragraph about policies related to own workforce using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Adopted workforce policies and their coverage
Non-discrimination, equal opportunities and diversity commitments
Occupational accident-prevention policy or management system
Policy implementation procedures when explicitly described
claim_risk_notes: Do not transfer supplier-worker policies to own workforce.
A policy commitment is not demonstrated implementation or effectiveness.
Do not extend a policy covering employees to all non-employees or all countries.
Do not infer alignment with international instruments from a generic commitment.
Do not infer policy absence from missing retrieved evidence.

tasks.task_name: Actions, resources and effectiveness related to own workforce
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about actions taken, underway or planned to address own-workforce impacts, risks and opportunities; resources, remediation, and evidenced methods or results for assessing effectiveness.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests implementation status, attribution, resources and claimed outcomes in workforce management. Routine training is included only when linked to a workforce impact, risk or opportunity.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS S1, paragraphs 35-43. Actions, resources and effectiveness related to own workforce.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: Historical workforce development, occupational health, inclusion, restructuring and employee-wellbeing narratives can provide action evidence. Numerical resource claims need a traceable table or passage.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about actions taken, underway or planned to address own-workforce impacts, risks and opportunities; resources, remediation, and evidenced methods or results for assessing effectiveness.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS S1-style disclosure paragraph about actions, resources and effectiveness related to own workforce using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Workforce actions taken, underway or planned
Actions addressing negative impacts and delivering positive impacts
Remediation and support for affected workers
Methods for tracking effectiveness and explicitly reported outcomes
claim_risk_notes: Do not turn planned activities into completed actions.
Do not infer causal improvement from participation or expenditure alone.
Do not assign a group-wide resource total to one workforce programme.
Do not treat a policy statement as evidence that an action occurred.
Separate workforce-development training from anti-corruption controls under G1-3.

tasks.task_name: Targets related to own-workforce impacts, risks and opportunities
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about time-bound and outcome-oriented workforce targets actually disclosed, including diversity or safety targets, baselines where stated, target dates, population boundaries, progress, and worker involvement in target setting.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Retains a substantive forward-looking workforce task. Both the 2023 standard and historical company reports support it; the selection is not based solely on symmetry with E1.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS S1, paragraphs 44-47; ESRS 2 MDR-T paragraphs 78-81. Targets related to own-workforce impacts, risks and opportunities.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: BASF 2023 discloses a 2030 target for women in leadership and a safety target. This establishes plausibility, not prevalence across the final sample. Targets require narrative or table evidence; the local numeric catalogue has no dedicated S1-5 entries.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about time-bound and outcome-oriented workforce targets actually disclosed, including diversity or safety targets, baselines where stated, target dates, population boundaries, progress, and worker involvement in target setting.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS S1-style disclosure paragraph about targets related to own-workforce impacts, risks and opportunities using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Diversity or occupational safety targets when disclosed
Target metric, target year and covered workforce population
Baseline values and years when disclosed
Worker or representative involvement in target-setting and monitoring when disclosed
claim_risk_notes: An ambition or policy commitment is not automatically a time-bound outcome target.
Preserve leadership-level and geographic boundaries.
Do not confuse a current result with a future target.
Do not invent baseline values, worker participation or external validation.
Separate target progress from causal effectiveness; preserve revisions to metric definitions.

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about health and safety management-system coverage, work-related fatalities, recordable accidents and their rates, work-related ill health and days lost, with worker category, metric definition and reporting period preserved.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Provides a quantitative and boundary-sensitive social task: employees versus non-employees, fatalities versus incidents, and incompatible accident-rate definitions require careful evidence use.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS S1, paragraphs 86-90; application requirements AR 80-95. Health and safety metrics.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue contains 23 indicator definitions, with nonempty extracted cells in 18 of 25 development company-years. These cells require source checking. Historical safety tables and methodology narratives are candidate sources.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about health and safety management-system coverage, work-related fatalities, recordable accidents and their rates, work-related ill health and days lost, with worker category, metric definition and reporting period preserved.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS S1-style disclosure paragraph about health and safety metrics using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Recordable work-related accidents and their rates
Work-related ill health and days lost
Metric definitions, rate denominators and hours worked
query_facets: health and safety management system coverage
claim_risk_notes: Do not equate LTIFR, TRIR, high-severity injury rates and ESRS recordable-accident rates.
Preserve rates per 200,000 versus 1,000,000 hours; do not silently convert or relabel.
Distinguish own-workforce non-employees from other workers at sites.
Do not infer zero fatalities or accidents from missing information.
Certification at selected sites does not establish group-wide coverage.
Do not equate accident counts, fatal events and numbers of people killed.

tasks.task_name: Business conduct policies and corporate culture
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about business-conduct policies, corporate culture, code of conduct, reporting channels, whistleblower protection, policy scope, and responsible functions.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests governance commitments and policy boundaries. Detailed anti-corruption procedures and training performance are reserved for G1-3.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 7-11. Business conduct policies and corporate culture.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: Historical codes of conduct and governance or compliance report sections are candidate sources. A hotline does not by itself establish anonymity, non-retaliation or independent investigation.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about business-conduct policies, corporate culture, code of conduct, reporting channels, whistleblower protection, policy scope, and responsible functions.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about business conduct policies and corporate culture using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Business-conduct policies and code of conduct
Development, promotion and assessment of corporate culture
Whistleblower protection and measures against retaliation
Animal-welfare policy where applicable and evidenced
claim_risk_notes: Do not infer an effective ethical culture from the existence of a code.
Distinguish confidential reporting, anonymity and protection against retaliation.
Do not infer independent investigation from an externally operated hotline.
Do not claim universal employee or supplier coverage without evidence.
Do not substitute board diversity or remuneration under ESRS 2 GOV for G1 business conduct.

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about supplier relationship management, procurement risks, social and environmental selection criteria, supplier assessment and development, and policies to prevent late payment, especially to SMEs.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Adds substantive supply-chain management coverage and prevents the four-task governance set from consisting entirely of internal compliance disclosures.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 12-15; application requirements AR 2-3. Management of relationships with suppliers.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: BASF and Evonik 2023 reports contain supplier selection, assessment, training and development evidence. The core is management practice; full payment-performance measurement belongs to G1-6.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about supplier relationship management, procurement risks, social and environmental selection criteria, supplier assessment and development, and policies to prevent late payment, especially to SMEs.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about management of relationships with suppliers using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Management of supplier relationships and procurement risks
Supplier engagement, development and corrective actions
Policies to prevent late payments, especially to SMEs
claim_risk_notes: An audit or assessment does not establish that every supplier complies.
Preserve direct versus indirect supplier and spend-versus-supplier-count denominators.
Do not attribute all industry-initiative audits to the company.
Supplier-worker impacts belong to S2 unless used specifically as evidence of procurement management.
A payment policy or a threshold such as paid within 60 days is not an observed average payment time.

tasks.task_name: Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery
tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery; investigator independence, reporting to governing bodies, policy communication and anti-corruption training.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Tests whether operational control and training claims are supported, while keeping allegations and incident outcomes in G1-4.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 16-21; application requirements AR 4-8. Prevention and detection of corruption and bribery.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue contains 21 training-related indicator definitions and nonempty extracted cells in all 25 development company-years. General compliance training must be distinguished from anti-corruption training.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery; investigator independence, reporting to governing bodies, policy communication and anti-corruption training.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about prevention and detection of corruption and bribery using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Procedures to prevent, detect, investigate and respond to corruption or bribery
Independence of investigators from implicated management
Reporting investigation outcomes to governing bodies
Communication of anti-corruption and anti-bribery policies
Nature, scope and depth of relevant training
Coverage of functions at risk and training of governing bodies
claim_risk_notes: Do not label all compliance training as anti-corruption training.
Do not confuse participants, unique people, completions, hours and coverage percentages.
Retain the correct denominator for functions at risk.
Do not infer control effectiveness or absence of corruption from training coverage.
Do not infer independence from an investigator's job title or external hotline operation.

tasks.task_scope: Retrieve evidence about reporting-period corruption and bribery convictions, fines and actions addressing breaches; confirmed incidents, disciplinary measures, business-partner consequences and legal-case outcomes when disclosed.
tasks.task_selection_rationale: Provides an incident-and-outcome task with substantively distinct allegation, confirmation and legal-status boundaries. Retention is conditional on a source audit because historical coverage is uneven.
tasks.official_requirement_basis: 2023 Annex I, ESRS G1, paragraphs 22-26. Incidents of corruption or bribery.
tasks.evidence_availability_rationale: The local catalogue has five indicator definitions and nonempty extracted cells in only 10 of 25 development company-years. Evonik 2023 demonstrates that extracted values can mislabel alleged cases and general compliance outcomes as confirmed corruption.
tasks.retrieval_intent: Find company-specific evidence about reporting-period corruption and bribery convictions, fines and actions addressing breaches; confirmed incidents, disciplinary measures, business-partner consequences and legal-case outcomes when disclosed.
tasks.generation_intent: Draft an ESRS G1-style disclosure paragraph about incidents of corruption or bribery using only the evidence available within the workflow boundary.
expected_evidence_content: Number of convictions and amounts of fines under anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws
Actions taken to address breaches in procedures and standards
Confirmed incidents and their nature where disclosed
Disciplinary measures, dismissals and business-partner consequences linked to corruption where disclosed
Public legal cases and reporting-period outcomes where disclosed
Incident status, reporting year, currency and company involvement
claim_risk_notes: Allegations, investigations, confirmed incidents and convictions are different statuses.
Do not treat all compliance dismissals or terminated contracts as corruption outcomes.
No convictions or no material cases does not establish no incidents.
Retain currency, reporting period, recognition basis and company involvement.
Do not treat missing evidence as zero, or a policy statement as an incident outcome.
A heading mentioning confirmed incidents cannot override qualifying text describing allegations.
